rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lahw means a pastime or play; the verbal noun is used in the sense of its object.
rows.anchor: ما يتلهى به ويلعب على أنه مصدر بمعنى المفعول

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: He glosses the pastime as something people play with and enjoy looking at, such as a woman or child.
rows.anchor: يزى بآن بازى كنند وبرؤية آن مستأنس شوند

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Lahw is whatever distracts a person from matters that concern him; it can describe any pleasurable diversion, while woman and child are only particular examples of worldly adornment.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب اللهو ما يشغل الإنسان عما يعنيه ويهمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jalalayn, transmitting Ibn Abbas, specifies a woman; Najm al-Din's Ta'wilat specifies both woman and child.
rows.anchor: المقصور على رواية ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Either a wife or child is a source of comfort, which explains calling them a man's two fragrant plants.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام الواحدي يستروح بكل واحد منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking something from God's presence means by divine power over all possible things, or from creatures He chooses, such as houris.
rows.anchor: من جهة قدرتنا عليه لتعلقها بكل شيء من المقدورات

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: From God's presence can mean privately and beyond human knowledge or control, as a man's wife and child are with him alone.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي معنى من لدنا من عندنا بحيث لا يظهر لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional means that if God were to do so, He would take it; the act is impossible because it conflicts with wisdom, not from inability.
rows.anchor: لكن تستحيل إرادتنا له لمنافاته الحكمة لا لعدم القدرة

rows.speaker: نجم الدين
rows.claim: The divine Presence and majesty are far above such impurities; the Creator is even more entitled to transcend what even honored angels avoid.
rows.anchor: جل جلال قدس حضرتنا عن أمثال هذه التدنسات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional إن is hypothetical, with its apodosis omitted because the preceding answer supplies it.
rows.anchor: وإن للشرط على سبيل الفرض والتقدير وجواب إن محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage turns from denying a child to God's usual action: He makes truth—seriousness, faith, and Quran—overcome falsehood such as play, disbelief, and other vanities.
rows.anchor: بل شأننا أن نغلب الحق الذي من جملته الجد والإيمان والقرآن

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Qadhf is a forceful throw over a distance, and falsehood is the opposite of truth because it has no stability when exposed.
rows.anchor: القذف الرمي البعيد ولاعتبار البعد فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadmugh means to destroy and eliminate.
rows.anchor: قال أهل التفسير إنما استعار لذلك أي :

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: They explain the image as a hard projectile of truth crushing hollow, soft falsehood like a brain struck through its membrane, making falsehood perish.
rows.anchor: قال أهل التفسير إنما استعار لذلك

rows.speaker: صاحب المفتاح
rows.claim: Qadhf and damgh first refer to bodies, then metaphorically to presenting truth to falsehood and erasing it; the sensory image makes the abstract scene vivid.
rows.anchor: قال "صاحب المفتاح" : أصل استعمال القذف والدمغ في الأجسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sudden particle and nominal sentence in fa-idha huwa zahiq signal how swiftly and completely falsehood disappears; the death image reinforces the metaphor.
rows.anchor: وفي إذا المفاجأة والجملة الإسمية من الدلالة على كمال المسارعة

rows.speaker: نجم الدين
rows.claim: There are three levels: God's commands defeat forbidden acts, manifestation of His attributes defeats servantly attributes, and manifestation of His Essence defeats all created essences.
rows.anchor: للحق ثلاث مراتب وكذا للباطل مرتبة أفعال الحق

rows.speaker: المغربي
rows.claim: The ecstatic utterance أنا الحق is explained as spoken when manifestation of the divine Essence or attribute makes the speaker's own false self vanish.
rows.anchor: لعل من قال أنا الحق إنما قال عند تجلي ذات الحق

rows.speaker: المغربي
rows.claim: His verse presents the speaker of أنا الحق as the servant whose defender and victor is the manifest Real.
rows.anchor: ناصر ومنصور ميكويد انا الحق المبين بشنواز ناصركه آن كفتار

rows.speaker: الخجندي
rows.claim: His verse associates hearing the secret أنا الحق with self-annihilation at the gallows of extinction.
rows.anchor: وقال الخجندي قدس سره : هركه بدار فنا جبه هستى بسوخت

rows.speaker: الخجندي
rows.claim: He says the secret of أنا الحق is lofty and cannot be understood without paying its price.
rows.anchor: أسرار أنا الحق سخهن نيك بلندست معنى نين جز بسردار نيابى

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Wayl can mean ugliness or woe and can express lament; ways is belittling and wayh expresses compassion.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي ويل قبوح وقد يستعمل في التحسر وويس استصغار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who call wayl a valley in Hell mean that the people God describes with it deserve a settled place in the Fire, not that this is the word's lexical meaning.
rows.anchor: ومن قال ويل واد في جهنم فإنه لم يرد أن ويلا في اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists are threatened with ruin because of their descriptions of God as having a woman or child and their accusations that revelation is magic, confused dreams, or similar falsehoods.
rows.anchor: من أجل وصفكم له سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause resumes the account of the apostate polytheist's great loss: he worships something besides God.
rows.anchor: استئناف مبين لعظم الخسران فيكون الضمير راجعا إلى المرتد المشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object worshipped can neither harm the worshipper if left alone nor benefit him when worshipped; the repeated ما underscores that it is an inert object.
rows.anchor: {ما لا يضره} إذا لم يعبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling this worship remote misguidance is a metaphor for a traveler lost in wilderness whose route grows longer and farther from the path.
rows.anchor: مستعارا من ضلال من أبعد في التيه ضالا عن الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing takes الدعاء as speech, the لام as introducing quoted words, and من as the subject of a clause describing whose harm is nearer than benefit; the oath-like curse is its predicate.
rows.anchor: الدعاء بمعنى القول واللام داخلة على الجملة الواقعة مقولا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse depicts the disbeliever crying out on Judgment Day after the idol harms him and he enters Hell without receiving any benefit; it confirms the fate and error of the earlier worship.
rows.anchor: حين يرى تضرره بمعبوده ودخوله النار بسببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the لام as extra and من as the object of يدعو, supported by a reading without the لام; worship harms him by bringing worldly killing and afterlife punishment, while expected intercession is only imagined, so the comparison is sarcastic.
rows.anchor: زائدة ومن مفعول يدعو ويؤيده القراءة بغير اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the thicket rejected Shuayb and the messengers before him.
rows.anchor: شعيبا ومن قبله عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ayka is a grove of soft-leaved trees near Midian, inhabited by a group of people.
rows.anchor: والأيكة الغيضة التي تنبت ناعم الشجر كالسدر والإدراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb was sent to them after his mission to Midian; he is called Midian's brother by kinship, but not the grove people's brother because he was unrelated to them.
rows.anchor: ولكن لما كان أخا مدين في النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives alternative genealogies for Shuayb: son of Tuwayb, son of Midyan, son of Abraham, or through Mikayk and Yashjar to Midyan and Abraham; Mikayk's mother was Lot's daughter.
rows.anchor: وهو شعيب بن تويب بن مدين بن إبراهيم أو ابن ميكيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb asks whether they fear the punishment of their Lord for associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: {ألا تتقون} (آيا نمي ترسيد از عذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is a trustworthy messenger among them, seeking only to set their affairs right.
rows.anchor: {إني لكم رسول أمين} بينكم وعلى الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should fear God and obey Shuayb because his command comes from God, so obeying him is obedience to God in reality.
rows.anchor: فإن أمري أمر عن الله وإطاعتي إطاعة الله في الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb asks no payment for delivering the message, teaching, or calling people; his reward and service fee are only with the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: أي على أداء الرسالة والتبليغ والتعليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All beneficence and good nurturing come from God, especially for someone charged with a divine command.
rows.anchor: فإن الفيض وحسن التربية منه تعالى على الكل خصوصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must complete the measure and not shortchange people's rights; خسرته and أخسرته mean that one made another's due deficient.
rows.anchor: {ولا تكونوا من المخسرين} حقوق الناس بالتطفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must weigh goods on a straight, fair scale; qistas can mean a scale, the most upright scales, or a Roman loanword for a balance.
rows.anchor: {بالقسطاس المستقيم} أي : بالميزان السوي العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb offers Moses one of his two daughters in marriage; the woman is identified as Safuriyya, the one linked with the fire episode.
rows.anchor: {إحدى ابنتى هاتين} (يكي را ازين دو دختران)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase أن تأجرني describes Moses becoming Shuayb's hired worker; the eight حجج are eight years.
rows.anchor: حال كونك مشروطا عليك أو واجبا أن تكون لي أجيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eight-year work is a condition owed to the father, not a dowry, since the wording says تأجرني rather than تأجرها; a marriage contract with a known work term for the guardian was permitted in Shuayb's law.
rows.anchor: وهذا شرط للأب وليس بصداق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A view reported in Ayn al-Maani says earlier laws let fathers receive their daughters' dowries, a rule abrogated in Islam by the command to give women their dowries.
rows.anchor: در شرائع متقدمه مهر اختران مر دررا بوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Islamic law a dowry must be valuable property and delivered to the woman; the author cites the commands to seek with wealth and to give women their dowries.
rows.anchor: وأن يكون مسلما إلى المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a free man marries for Quran teaching or a year's service, the marriage is valid but the proper equivalent dowry is due because teaching or free labor is not property; a slave's service can count because his person is delivered.
rows.anchor: فلو تزوجها على تعليم القرآن أو خدمته لها سنة يصح النكاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either reading—dowry or condition—the verse concerns Shuayb's law; in current law the dowry belongs to the woman, and Abu Hanifa disallows a condition that draws the dowry's benefit to the father, unlike al-Shafii.
rows.anchor: فالآية سواء حملت على الصداق أو على الشرط فناظرة إلى شريعة شعيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the account simply states what Shuayb and Moses intended and agreed to do, without ruling on the legal basis of either arrangement in their law.
rows.anchor: ما حكي عنهما بيان لما عزما عليه واتفقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspired Moses in a dream to strike the watering-place with his staff; the sheep then bore the specified lambs, showing Shuayb that this was provision from God for Moses and his wife, so he fulfilled the agreement and handed over the flock.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله إليه في المنام أن اضرب بعصاك الماء الذي هو في مستقى الأغنام

rows.speaker: أبو الليث
rows.claim: Such a condition is not binding in Islamic law, but a prophet's promise is binding, so Moses fulfilled his promise.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الليث : مثل هذا الشرط في شريعتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited Mathnawi verse teaches that fidelity is a companion whose good or evil follows one into the grave.
rows.anchor: باوفاتر از عمل نبود رفيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses completed both agreements and the work term; a report says he chose the longer term, ten years.
rows.anchor: فلما أتم الأجل المشروط بينهما وفرغ منه روي أنه قضى أبعد الأجلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb grieved at Moses's departure in his old age; Moses said he had been long absent from his mother, aunt, Aaron, and sister in Pharaoh's kingdom.
rows.anchor: يا موسى كيف تخرج عني وقد ضعفت وكبرت؟ فقال له : قد طالت غيبتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb prayed by the honor of Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph for his strength and sight to be restored; Moses said amen and God restored them.
rows.anchor: يا رب بحرمة إبراهيم الخليل وإسماعيل الصفي وإسحاق الذبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses traveled toward Egypt with Shuayb's permission; سير means to move through the land.
rows.anchor: موسى بإذن شعيب نحو مصر والسير المضي في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His أهل were his wife Safuriyya and their child, whom she bore before the journey, according to Kashf al-Asrar; Kashifi reads the باء as causative, “he took his family.”
rows.anchor: {بأهله} بامرأته صفوريا وولده

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Esoterically, after Moses completed the term of love and nearness approached, he traveled with his family so they could share in the subtleties of divine beneficence.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : لما تم له أجل المحبة

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: It was a dark, cold night with rain and snow; Moses camped by a valley, his sheep scattered in the storm, and his pregnant wife went into labor. He tried to kindle a fire but could not.
rows.anchor: وكان في البرية والليلة مظلمة باردة فضرب خيمته على الوادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses saw a fire from the direction facing the mountain; جانب means the side toward something, and al-Tur is a particular mountain; النار can denote visible flame, bare heat, or Hellfire.
rows.anchor: أبصر من الجهة التي تلي الطور نارا يقال جانب الحائط للجهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Moses saw fire as a sign of lights: divine light appeared dressed as fire to match his need and familiar desire in winter; Gabriel likewise often appeared as Dihya because the Prophet loved him.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : أبصر نارا دالة على الأنوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker of قال is Moses.
rows.anchor: {قال} موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amkuthu means to remain and wait, so Moses told his family to stay where they were.
rows.anchor: المكث ثبات مع انتظار أي قفوا مكانكم واثبتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He hoped to bring news from people by the fire about which way led to Egypt, since the travelers had lost their route.
rows.anchor: بيامي يعني از نزد كساني كه برسر آن آتش اند بيارم خبر طريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jadhwa is a thick piece of wood, whether or not it still has fire; al-Mufradat defines it as wood remaining after burning.
rows.anchor: عود غليظ سواء كانت في رأسه نار أو لا

rows.speaker: نجم الدين
rows.claim: The journey signifies outward detachment from family, property, and the world, and inward separation from attachment to both worlds; as attachment falls away, signs of unity appear, first as Moses's flame or Abraham's star, then as flashes, suns, and moons until the light of lordship appears.
rows.anchor: تشير الآية إلى التجريد في الظاهر وإلى التفريد في الباطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iṣṭilā means warming oneself at a fire; the noun ṣalāʾ has alternative vowelings and corresponding short or long forms.
rows.anchor: الاصطلاء التدفؤ بالصلاء وهو النار بفتح الصاد وكسرها

rows.speaker: نجم الدين
rows.claim: Human qualities are frozen by nature's cold and warm only through the spark of love or the fire of divine attraction.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أن أوصاف الإنسانية جامدة من برودة الطبيعة

rows.speaker: الكمال الخجندي
rows.claim: His verse says a heart that has not burned in love is unworthy of the beloved's gaze.
rows.anchor: دلي كه سوخته آتش محبت نيست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses left his family and went to the fire; when he arrived, the call came from the right bank relative to him, a place where water flows between mountains, hence called a valley.
rows.anchor: فترك موسى أهله في البرية وذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed spot is the place where Moses first received the message and God's speech; the author compares it with places of divine manifestation for saints.
rows.anchor: وصفت بكونها مباركة لأنه حصل فيها ابتداء الرسالة وتكليم الله إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every soul, whether human or otherwise, is included; the generic indefinite noun is valid because it conveys universality.
rows.anchor: من النفوس سواء كان نفس الإنسان أو غيرها وهو مبتدأ وجاز الابتداء بالنكرة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Tasting death means experiencing its bitterness and the pangs of separation; this assumes tasting can refer to little or much.
rows.anchor: وهذا مبني على أن الذوق يصلح للقليل والكثير كما ذهب إليه الراغب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes tasting literally as a small amount taken by mouth: souls undergo a portion of death through contact with the body.
rows.anchor: أصل الذوق بالفم فيما يقل تناوله فالمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A human consists of body, soul, and a subtle vapor between them called the animal spirit; life continues while this connection remains viable, then ends when it extinguishes and the soul involuntarily leaves the body, a formal death.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الإنسان روحا وجسدا وبخارا لطيفا بينهما هو الروح الحيواني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those who have fully disengaged from ordinary attachment know how the spirit appears in the body and departs at death.
rows.anchor: ولا يعرف كيفية ظهور الروح في البدن ومفارقته له وقت الموت إلا أهل الانسلاخ التام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning to God means returning to His judgment and recompense.
rows.anchor: {ثم إلينا} أي إلى حكمنا وجزائنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turja'un derives from raj' and means that you are returned.
rows.anchor: {ترجعون} من الرجع وهو الرد أي تردون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since this is the final outcome, people should prepare for it and regard leaving home and exile as easy when their homeland is a land of idolatry or sin and innovation they cannot change; they should migrate to a land of obedience.
rows.anchor: فمن كانت هذه عاقبته ينبغي أن يجتهد في التزود والاستعداد لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Migration for the sake of religion is among the righteous deeds of those who believe and act well.
rows.anchor: ومن الصالحات الهجرة للدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lanubawwi'annahum means We will settle them; al-Taj defines the root as placing someone in a place.
rows.anchor: قال في "التاج" : النبوء (كسى را جابي فرآوردن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chambers are lofty palaces of pearl, emerald, and ruby; Heaven is above while Hell is below, and viewing water and greenery from a chamber is especially delightful.
rows.anchor: قصورا عالية من الدر والزبرجد والياقوت وإنما قال ذلك لأن الجنة في جهة عالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase streams beneath them describes the chambers, and the believers remain there forever.
rows.anchor: صفة لغرفا {خالدين فيها} أي : ماكثين في تلك الغرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The excellent reward is for people who perform righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: {نعم أجر العاملين} الأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those described as patient modify “the workers,” or are an accusative of praise; their patience covers persecution, migration's hardship, and other trials.
rows.anchor: صفة للعاملين أو نصب على المدح أي صبروا على أذية المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They rely only on God; strong faith loosens attachment to homeland, property, and provision, makes exile and home alike, and leaves God's reward sufficient.
rows.anchor: لا يعتمدون في أمورهم إلا على الله تعالى وهذا التوكل من قوة الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says that someone who flees with his religion even a short distance merits Paradise and companionship with Abraham and Muhammad; he merits Paradise for giving up home for religion and their company by following their migration and reviving their practice.
rows.anchor: من فر بدينه من أرض إلى أرض ولو كان شبرا استوجب الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the spiritual traveler, migration means leaving the land of social prestige and public acceptance for obscurity.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن السالك ينبغي أن يهاجر من أرض الجاه

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
rows.claim: When his reputation became so great that people competed to buy a melon that fell from his hand, he left; he was content to live where people called him an unbeliever and stoned him twice a day.
rows.anchor: حكايت كنند از ابو سعيد خراز قدس سره كفت در شهرى بودم

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
rows.claim: He said he had felt worldly joy only three times; in Antioch he went barefoot and bareheaded, welcomed being called a runaway slave, and told his self that if it had fled, it could now return peacefully.
rows.anchor: واز ابراهيم ادهم قدس سره حكايت كنند كه كفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to endure his opponents' verbal and physical abuse; God's promise to give him victory and manifest his religion is true and certain to be fulfilled.
rows.anchor: {فاصبر} يا محمد على أذاهم قولا وفعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yastakhiffannak means not to let them unsettle or distress him.
rows.anchor: لا يحملنك على الخفة والقلق جزعا

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: The phrase means do not let their doubts agitate you or dislodge you from your belief.
rows.anchor: لا يزعجنك ولا يزيلنك عن اعتقادك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers lack certainty, deny the signs, and use false accusations such as calling the messengers liars; such behavior is expected from doubters astray.
rows.anchor: فإنهم شاكّون ضالون ولا يستبدع منهم أمثال ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the wording appears to forbid the unbelievers from undermining the Prophet, it indirectly forbids him from being affected by their contempt.
rows.anchor: فظاهر النظم الكريم وإن كان نهيا للكفرة عن استخفافه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Abu Talib died, Quraysh intensified their abuse; one fool threw dust on the Prophet's head, and when his daughter wept while wiping it away he reassured her that God would protect him. The Companions also endured abuse and ultimately prevailed.
rows.anchor: روي أنه لما مات أبو طالب عم النبي عليه السلام بالغ قريش في الأذى

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: His verse urges steadfastness in love because this path does not go unrewarded.
rows.anchor: دلادر عاشقى ثابت قدم باش كه دراين ره نباشد كار بى اجر

rows.speaker: نجم الدين
rows.claim: For a sincere seeker, patience means disciplining the self away from familiar desires, guarding the heart from ego traits, and helping the spirit give up its existence to receive divine generosity.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى الطالب الصادق فاصبر على مقاساة شدائد فطام النفس

rows.speaker: نجم الدين
rows.claim: God's true promise to the seeker is expressed as: whoever seeks Me will find Me.
rows.anchor: فيما قال : "ألا من طلبني وجدني"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also warns against idle people who belittle truth-seekers as ignorant; even those with inherited faith may lack certainty and try to block seekers with mockery and denial.
rows.anchor: يشير به إلى استخفاف أهل البطالة واستجهالهم أهل الحق وطلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such critics deny that seeking God is obligatory and scorn those who leave worldly life, family, and children for the quest.
rows.anchor: لأنهم لا يوقنون بوجوب طلب الحق تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seeker first needs outward detachment, then inward separation of the heart from attachment to happiness in either world; by these two steps people reach unity.
rows.anchor: ويجب على طالبي الحق أولا التجريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited saying summarizes the path as two steps followed by arrival.
rows.anchor: كما قال بعضهم خطوتان وقد وصلت

rows.speaker: العطار
rows.claim: His poem compares annihilation of the self to a clod falling into the sea: once the clod loses its separate self, only the sea remains; while it insists on itself, it cannot find union.
rows.anchor: مكرسنك وكلوخى بود درراه بدريايى در افتادند ناكاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mathnawi story of a grammarian and a boatman teaches that grammar cannot save the scholar from drowning; self-effacement is needed, and the sea carries the dead while the living may drown.
rows.anchor: ليك اندم كرد خاموش از جواب باد كشتى را بكردابى فكند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The son is called An'am, by which Luqman is also known as Abu An'am.
rows.anchor: انعم فهو أبو أنعم أي : يكنى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman admonishes his son; admonition is a rebuke joined with warning, while al-Khalil defines it as a reminder of good that softens the heart.
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل : هو التذكير بالخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The diminutive يا بني conveys tenderness and affection, fitting advice intended for the son's happiness if he follows it.
rows.anchor: وهو تصغير رحمة وعطوفة ولهذا أوصاه بما فيه سعادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk means treating something besides God as His partner in worship; it is immense injustice because it equates the source of every favor with one that gives no favor.
rows.anchor: لا تعدل بالله شيئا في العبادة

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Shirk is injustice against oneself, and its gravity lies in its never being forgiven.
rows.anchor: في "كشف الأسرار" (بيدادى است برخويشتن بزرك) وعظمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman's son and wife were initially unbelievers but became Muslim through his efforts; unlike Noah's son and wife, Lot's daughters accepted faith while his wife did not and was turned to stone in one report.
rows.anchor: وكان ابنه وامرأته كافرين فما زال بهما حتى أسلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Luqman began his advice with the warning to avoid shirk.
rows.anchor: وعظ لقمان ابنه في ابتداء وعظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, admonition turns the self from what is below God and gives God alone the soul's service, the heart's attention, and the spirit's vision; this is individuation within unity.
rows.anchor: والوعظ زجر النفس عن الاشتغال بما دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to honor parents interrupts Luqman's advice and reinforces its prohibition of shirk.
rows.anchor: اعتراض في أثناء وصية لقمان تأكيدا لما فيها من النهي عن الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage highlights the mother's right and the parents' great claim: she carried the child through weakness upon weakness, then nursed until weaning.
rows.anchor: ثم رجح الأم ونبه على عظم حق والديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahn is weakness in constitution and character; as the fetus grows, the mother's weakness increases until delivery.
rows.anchor: والوهن الضعف من حيث الخلق والخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fisal is separation from nursing, as a camel calf is called fasīl when weaned from its mother.
rows.anchor: الفصال التفريق بين الصبي والرضاع ومنه الفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text distinguishes عام as often associated with ease from سنة, often used for hardship or drought; weaning is completed at two years from birth.
rows.anchor: لكن كثيرا ما تستعمل السنة في الحول الذي فيه الشدة والجدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For al-Shafii, suckling through two years establishes milk kinship; it is obligatory until the child is self-sufficient, recommended through two years, and permissible through two and a half, while the disagreement concerns milk kinship.
rows.anchor: وهي مدة الرضاع عند الشافعي فلا يثبت حرمة الرضاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By agreement, the father's nursing-wage obligation is limited to two years and does not continue afterward.
rows.anchor: أما استحقاق الأجرة فمقدر بحولين فلا تجب نفقة الإرضاع

rows.speaker: الوسيط
rows.claim: The verse recalls the mother's hardship in nursing the child for two years after birth.
rows.anchor: قال في الوسيط : المعنى ذكر مشقة الوالدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ushkur li either explains the command to thank God or gives its purpose; the intervening words particularly reinforce the duty to the mother.
rows.anchor: تفسير لوصيناه أي : قلنا له اشكر لي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When asked whom to honor most, the Prophet answered “your mother” three times, then “your father.”
rows.anchor: لمن قال له من أبر "أمك ثم أمك ثم أمك"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thank God for creating and guiding you to Islam, and thank parents for raising you; gratitude to God is reverence and glorification, while gratitude to parents is compassion and respect.
rows.anchor: اشكر لي حيث أوجدتك وهديتك بالإسلام واشكر لوالديك حيث ربيّاك صغيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharh al-Hikam says their gratitude is joined to God's because parents are the proximate, figurative cause of existence, while God is its true source.
rows.anchor: قرن شكرهما بشكره إذ هما أصل وجودك المجازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith that one who does not thank people does not thank God means either that thanking people is a condition for valid gratitude to God or that God's reward goes only to those who thank His servants.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "لا يشكر الله من لا يشكر الناس" فجعل شكر الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A teacher's right to gratitude exceeds a parent's; Alexander says his father brought him down from heaven to earth while his tutor raised him from earth to heaven.
rows.anchor: ثم حق المعلم في الشكر فوق حق الوالدين

rows.speaker: برزجمهر
rows.claim: He says he honors his teacher more because his father caused his mortal life, while his teacher caused his lasting life.
rows.anchor: لبرزجمهر ما بالك تعظيمك لمعلمك أشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return to God explains why obedience is required: people return to Him alone and He will reward gratitude or ingratitude.
rows.anchor: تعليل لوجوب الامتثال بالأمر أي : إلى الرجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning to God means reaching a state where no judge or owner exists but Him.
rows.anchor: الرجوع إلى الله الرجوع إلى حيث لا حاكم ولا مالك سواه

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: He says the five daily prayers thank God, while praying for one's parents after those prayers thanks them.
rows.anchor: قال سفيان بن عيينة : من صلى الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that honoring a deceased father includes maintaining ties with his friends; if parents died while one was undutiful, prayer and charity for them afterward can restore filial piety.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "من أحب أن يصل أباه في قبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report from al-Ihya and Qut al-Qulub prescribes two Thursday-night rakahs with specified repeated recitations, followed by fifteen istighfars dedicated to parents; it says this fulfills their right even for a disobedient child.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "من صلى ليلة الخميس ما بين المغرب والعشاء ركعتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mujahada means expending one's utmost capacity to resist an enemy; if parents press someone to associate partners with God without grounds, the child must not obey them, since filial service never permits sin.
rows.anchor: المجاهدة استفراغ الجهد أي : الوسع في مدافعة العدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited Persian verse says that if religion and piety are lacking, cutting kinship is preferable to affection for relatives.
rows.anchor: ون نبود خويش را ديانت وتقوى قطع رحم بهتر از مودت قربى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Still, one should keep good company with parents in worldly matters through proper conduct and generosity, including spending on them.
rows.anchor: صحابا {معروفا} ومعاشرة جميلة يرتضيه الشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith defines good companionship as feeding parents when hungry and clothing them when unclothed.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "حسن المصاحبة أن يطعمهما إذا جاعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims must support, honor, serve, and visit non-Muslim parents too; if they might draw the child into unbelief, he may avoid visits or taking them to church and may bring them home from it.
rows.anchor: فيجب على المسلم نفقة الوالدين ولو كانا كافرين وبرهما وخدمتهما وزيارتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the recognized good here includes correcting parents who are ignorant about God and mistaken in religion.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : المعروف ههنا أن يعرفهما

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Ma'ruf names what reason and revealed law recognize as good, while munkar is what they reject; moderation in generosity is called ma'ruf.
rows.anchor: قال في "المفردات" : المعروف اسم لكل فعل يعرف بالعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Follow the way of those who turn to God in monotheism and sincere obedience, namely complete believers; at the return He will disclose and recompense each person's deeds.
rows.anchor: {واتبع} في الدين {سبيل من أناب إلى} رجع بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas after he embraced Islam and his mother swore not to eat or drink until he returned to her religion.
rows.anchor: ونزلت الآية في سعد بن أبي وقاص رضي الله عنه من العشرة المبشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman addresses his son An'am affectionately as “my son”; the name is vocalized with a damma on the عين.
rows.anchor: (كفت لقمان فرزند خودرا كه انعم نام بود)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining counsel continues the opening warning against shirk, as described in al-Irshad.
rows.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : شروع في حكاية بقية وصايا لقمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine “it” refers to a deed, whether sinful or good.
rows.anchor: أي : الخصلة من الإساءة أو الإحسان

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Luqman's son asked how God would know of a sin committed where no one could see him; Luqman answered that even the mustard-seed deed is known to God.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل وذلك أن ابن لقمان قال لأبيه : يا أبتاه إن عملت

rows.speaker: نجم الدين
rows.claim: Persevering in prayer means persisting in leaving indecency and wrongdoing: whoever avoids them is in prayer even without its outward form, while performing the form without restraint is not truly in prayer.
rows.anchor: أدمها وإدامتها في أن تنتهي عن الفحشاء والمنكر

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: When fasting, one should eat enough bread to curb desire rather than lose strength and miss prayer, which God values more than fasting.
rows.anchor: اى سر روزه كه دارى نان دار كه شهوت ببرد نه قوت ببرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting and ascetic disciplines improve temperament and character, while prayer reforms the soul, the dwelling of evil and the source of desire; no worshipped object is more hateful to God than desire.
rows.anchor: وأما الصلاة فلإصلاح النفس التي هي مأوى كل شر ومعدن كل هوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma'ruf is what reason and law approve; in its true sense it leads a servant to God. Munkar is what they condemn and what distracts from God.
rows.anchor: {وأمر بالمعروف} بالمستحسن شرعا وعقلا وحقيقته ما يوصل العبد إلى الله {وانه عن المنكر} أي : عن المستقبح شرعا وعقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience restrains the self from what law or reason requires it to avoid and bears illness, poverty, grief, and especially abuse received while commanding good and forbidding evil.
rows.anchor: الصبر حبس النفس عما يقتضي الشرع أو العقل الكف عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” refers to enjoining good, forbidding wrong, and patience; these are matters of firm resolve, without doubt or resistance.
rows.anchor: {إن ذالك} المذكور من الوصايا وهو الأمر والنهي والصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azm means a settled determination; “matters of resolve” can mean obligations God decisively commanded or, grammatically, matters that are themselves resolute.
rows.anchor: وعزم الأمور ما لا يشوبه شبهة ولا يدافعه ريبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report about four prayers before Asr and the supplication for “resolutions of forgiveness” interprets azm as a sure, binding promise or as deeds that necessarily bring forgiveness.
rows.anchor: من صلى قبل العصر أربعا غفر الله له مغفرة عزما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verse says tribulation brings nearness and friendship with God, while patience, piety, and obedience to the Lord rank highest for mystics.
rows.anchor: صبر وتقوى وطاعت مولى نزد عارف زهر شرف اولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial إنّا uses a majestic plural nūn according to scholars; knowers instead see the nūn as indicating the plurality of divine names and attributes.
rows.anchor: هذه النون نون العظمة والكبرياء عند العلماء فإن الملوك والعظماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains عرض in its senses of appearing, presenting something, offering goods for sale, or inspecting troops; amāna is the opposite of betrayal and is what has been entrusted.
rows.anchor: عرض لي أمر كذا أي : ظهر وعرضت له الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first of three levels of trust is the religious and legal obligations, called a trust because they must be received obediently and fulfilled.
rows.anchor: المرتبة الأولى : أنها التكاليف الشرعية والأمور الدينية المرعية

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Religious duties are entrusted rights placed with accountable people, who must accept, preserve, and perform them fully.
rows.anchor: عبر عن التكاليف الشرعية بالأمانة لأنها حقوق مرعية أودعها الله المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This first trust includes intellect, which enables human learning and good action and distinguishes people; it also includes faith and worship, honesty, guarding speech and secrets, repaying debts, fair measures, ritual purity, good prayer, patience, gratitude, vows, chastity, the senses, and all duties required by law.
rows.anchor: وتلك الأمانة هي العقل أولا فإن به يحصل تعلم كل ما في طوق البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The primordial covenants were placed in the Black Stone, which is chief among gems and God's custodian of the trust.
rows.anchor: صورة المسمى بالحجر الأسود لسيادته بين الجواهر وألقمه الحق تلك المواثيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second level is divine love, ardor, and attraction, the fruit of the first trust; it distinguishes humans from angels because trials and difficult obligations permit human ascent.
rows.anchor: والمرتبة الثانية : أنها المحبة والعشق والانجذاب الإلهي

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: His poem's dark night signifies divine majesty, fear of waves the awe of overpowering attributes, and the whirlpool the frightening trials and barriers in love's sea; angels and ascetics remain lightly burdened at its shore.
rows.anchor: أراد بقوله : "شب تاريك" جلال الذات وبقوله : "بيم موج" خوف صفات القهر

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: His other verse says angels do not know the story of love and asks that a cup be poured on Adam's earth.
rows.anchor: فرشته عشق نداندكه يست قصه مخوان

rows.speaker: المولى الجامي
rows.claim: His couplet says the angels benefit from excellent worship, while the grace of love was poured upon Adam.
rows.anchor: وقول المولى الجامي : ملائك را ه سود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawami says angels lack humanity's painful love and trials; without suffering, love has no worth. Humans bearing the description “corrupting on earth” and “unjust, ignorant” can endure the wine of trial because the heart bears what the body cannot.
rows.anchor: محبت بى دردرا قدر وقيمتى نيست عشق را طائفة در خورند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third level is divine effusion without intermediary, which no one owns; it comes through removing existential veils by annihilation in the Reality and subsistence through Lordship, as the fulfillment of love and the level of the divine Essence.
rows.anchor: والمرتبة الثالثة أنها الفيض الإلهي بلا واسطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At this level the heart gives birth to God's deputy on earth who bears the trust; the three levels belong respectively to common people, the elect, and the most elect, with each level's inner core leading to the next.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا المقام يتولد من القلب طفل خليفة الله في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's shaykh said that food has a divine spirit as well as bodily substance; the body and spirit are strengthened together, as the Mathnawi says lawful food increases wisdom, love, and refinement.
rows.anchor: فقال أثناء الإفطار أن لهذا الخبر روحا حقانيا فظاهره يرجع إلى الجسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every existent has either an animal or divine spirit; even a dead body retains divine spirit apart from the animal spirit, and all things truly glorify God because life runs through them.
rows.anchor: ولكل موجود روح إما حيواني أو حقاني فجسد الميت له روح حقاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples of this life in creation include mountains praising with David, wind carrying Solomon, earth swallowing Qarun, the Prophet's mosque trunk moaning, and a stone greeting the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ولذا سبح الجبال مع داود وحمل الريح سليمان عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mathnawi verses chide people for treating beings as lifeless and missing the speech of the world's parts.
rows.anchor: ون شما سوى جمادى مى رويد محرم جان جمادان ون شويد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that God placed reason and understanding in the inanimate things when He offered them the trust, just as He did in Solomon's ant, the hoopoe, animals, stones, trees, and soil; they heard and answered His question about reward for keeping the trust and punishment for betrayal.
rows.anchor: والوجه الثاني أن الله تعالى ركب العقل والفهم في الجمادات المذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens, earth, and mountains refused from fear that they would fail the trust and be punished, not from disobedience; the offer was optional, since obligatory refusal would merit blame, which God did not impose.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن هذا القول منهن من جهة المعصية والمخالفة بل من جهة الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains said they were subject to divine command and sought neither reward nor punishment; their refusal came from fear of failing the trust, not disobedience.
rows.anchor: والمعنى وخفن من الأمانة وحملها وقلن يا رب نحن مسخرات بأمرك لا نريد ثوابا ولا عقابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative treats the offer as a hypothetical parable: their lack of capacity is pictured as refusal and fear, and the trust's greatness as a heavy physical burden that even enormous self-aware bodies would decline.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : أنه محمول على الفرض والتمثيل

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: He distinguishes the mountains' voluntary offer, which they declined, from the human's imposed duty, which he undertook.
rows.anchor: كما قال الإمام القشيري (أمانتها برانها عرض نمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity means the human race; it accepted the trust despite weak bodily constitution because carrying it requires resolve, not physical strength.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالإنسان الجنس بدليل قوله : {إنه كان ظلوما جهولا}

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Carrying the trust means either accepting it through innate capacity or acknowledging it at the primordial covenant by saying بلى.
rows.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : وهو إما عبارة عن قبولها بموجب استعداده الفطري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the claim that God carried people on land and sea and that the reward for excellence is excellence; an analogy says weak trees bear the heaviest, sweetest fruit because divine care supports the weak.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى : {وحملناهم في البر والبحر} (الإسراء : 70) {هل جزاء الإحسان إلا الإحسان} (الرحمن : 60)

rows.speaker: جنيد
rows.claim: Junayd says Adam looked at God's bestowal rather than the trust's burden, so the joy of the gift made him forget its weight; divine grace said that lifting was Adam's choice while preservation was God's.
rows.anchor: شيخ جنيد قدس سره (فرموده كه نظر آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Adam asked whether to carry the trust by his own strength or through God; he was told that whoever bears what comes from God can bear it only through God.
rows.anchor: وروي أن آدم عليه السلام قال : أحمل الأمانة بقوتي أم بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian verse says that the burden can be borne only with God's help; another says the throne refused it but a human can carry it by divine power.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : آن باركه ازبردن آن عرش ابا كرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human alone was fit to bear this immense trust and the mantle of the earthly vicegerent announced in the creation of Adam; the trust's appointment exposed the envy of the devils.
rows.anchor: خلعت حمل امانت جز برقامت با استقامت انسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is unjust to itself through disobedience and failure to fulfill the trust, and ignorant of the consequences of betraying it.
rows.anchor: لنفسه بمعصية ربه حيث لم يف بالأمانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zulm means putting something outside its proper place by deficiency, excess, or wrong time or location; the author illustrates the term with taking milk too early and digging ground where it should not be dug.
rows.anchor: والظلم وضع الشيء في غير موضعه المختص به إما بنقصان أو بزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term applies to small or great transgression, so Adam and Iblis can both be called unjust despite the vast difference between their wrongs.
rows.anchor: ولذا قيل لآدم في تقدمه ظالم وفي إبليس ظالم وإن كان بين الظلمين بون بعيد

rows.speaker: بعض الحكماء
rows.claim: One classification begins with injustice between a person and God, whose gravest forms are unbelief, shirk, and hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الحكماء : الظلم ثلاثة : أحدهما : بين الإنسان وبين الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites and polytheists are punished for betraying the trust: hypocrites accepted it and then neglected it, while polytheists betrayed it by refusing it outright; believers who preserved it are granted repentance.
rows.anchor: الذين ضيعوا الأمانة بعدما قبلوها {والمشركين والمشركات} الذين خانوا في الأمانة بعدم قبولها

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: The لام can mark consequence: some humans accepted the trust but failed to obey, so punishment followed even though it was not God's purpose in offering it.
rows.anchor: على أن اللام للعاقبة فإن التعذيب وإن لم يكن غرضا له من الحمل

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Alternatively, the لام gives the purpose of offering the trust: it revealed hypocrites' and polytheists' condition so they could be punished.
rows.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" : ويجوز أن تكون اللام علة لعرضنا

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Repentance is the outcome for believers who kept the trust: God accepts their return because they did not abandon obedience completely and they repair human slips through repentance.
rows.anchor: الذين حفظوا الأمانة وراعوا حقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit mention of God's name first heightens awe; naming Him again instead of using a pronoun emphasizes care for believers and gives warning and promise their due.
rows.anchor: والالتفات إلى الاسم الجليل أولا لتهويل الخطب وتربية المهابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is abundant in forgiveness and mercy: He forgives believers' lapses and rewards their obedience with success.
rows.anchor: مبالغا في المغفرة والرحمة حيث تاب عليهم وغفر لهم فرطاتهم

rows.speaker: نجم الدين
rows.claim: The closing lam marks consequence: the wisdom of offering the trust is that creation falls into three classes.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : هذه اللام لام الصيرورة والعاقبة يشير إلى أن الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “My servants” tells the believers to repeat these words exactly; the divine possessive address honors them, with the ياء omitted because the preceding kasra suffices.
rows.anchor: قل لهم قولي هذا بعينه وفيه تشريف لهم بإضافتهم إلى ضمير الجلالة

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: The address is to people who aligned themselves with the Real and preferred God's pleasure to the ego's desire, thereby attaining true servanthood and the title “My servants.”
rows.anchor: اين خطاب يا قومي است كه مراد نفس خويش بموافقت حق بدادند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet says that whoever despises his self for God's sake will be protected by God from the punishment of Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: ومصطفى عليه السلام كفت "من مقت نفسه في ذات الله آمنه الله

rows.speaker: أبو يزيد
rows.claim: Abu Yazid says that if asked to choose at the resurrection, he would ask to be thrown into Hell so he could present his self there, having suffered from it in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وأبو يزيد بسطامى قدس سره ميكويد اكر فرادى قيامت مرا كويند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most elect servants are freed from servitude to everything besides God, including this world and the next; they believe in God through longing and love as seekers.
rows.anchor: إن أخص الخواص هم العباد الذين خلصوا من عبودية الغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittaqu rabbakum can mean remain firm in piety, fear God's punishment through obedience and avoidance of sin, or use God as protection from everything besides Him to escape separation and attain union and the joy of His beauty.
rows.anchor: اثبتوا على تقوى ربكم ، لأن الإيمان حصول التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who do good in this world perform righteous acts sincerely; the chief good deed is the testimony of faith.
rows.anchor: عملوا الأعمال الحسنة في هذه الدنيا على وجه الإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, حسنة is the subject, للذين its predicate, and فى هذه الدنيا modifies أحسنوا.
rows.anchor: حسنة} : مبتدأ وخبره للذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise alludes to the world as a farm for the next life: the great reward is Paradise and vision of God, whose reality is beyond knowing.
rows.anchor: قوله : "الدنيا مزرعة الآخرة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihsan is to worship as though seeing God, knowing that He sees you; the true doer of good witnesses God, so other things disappear and sincerity is complete, while one attached to other-than-God risks shirk and ostentation.
rows.anchor: الإحسان أن تعبد الله ، كأنك تراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bad deed cannot earn a good reward.
rows.anchor: ومن كان عمله قبيحا لم يكن جزاؤه حسنا

rows.speaker: نجم الدين
rows.claim: The verse points to people who do good in seeking God and ask no good from anyone else; their good is finding God, which is deposited within sincere seeking.
rows.anchor: في "التأويلات النجمية" : {للذين أحسنوا} في طلبي

rows.speaker: الخجندي
rows.claim: His poem says to strive for the key to the treasure of existence, since the desired jewel cannot be found without seeking, and the lovers' end is blessed.
rows.anchor: حسن الوجدان مودع في حسن الطلب : قال الخجندي :
